LESSON MENU
CONVERSION CIRCUITS
An Analog to Digital (A/D) converter is a circuit that changes analog signals to digital signals.
DISCUSSION
A Digital to Analog (D/A) converter is a circuit that changes digital signals to analog signals.
This is a simultaneous A/D converter circuit or flash converter.
This circuit compares the analog input voltage with a reference voltage produced by R1 through R4.
When the analog voltage exceeds the reference voltage for a given comparator, a high is generated.
The high or low outputs of the comparators are applied to an encoder which produces a two-digit binary number on every sampling pulse..
The output of the encoder represents the digital equivalent to the analog input.
An analog sine wave produces a digital square wave represented in binary numbers.
The advantage of this type of A/D converter is that the analog input is converted to digital simultaneously.
An important fact to remember is that a separate comparator is needed for each level of quantization. This can be considered a disadvantage when there is limited space for circuit components.
An important fact to remember is that a separate comparator is needed for each level of quantization. This can be considered a disadvantage when there is limited space for circuit components.
QUANTIZATION - the assignment of a unique value from a range of digital values (set by the number of bits used) based on the sampling of an analog waveform.
DEFINITION
This is a stairstep A/D converter, or ramp converter.......
The analog input is compared with the output of a D/A converter.
If the analog input voltage is higher than the output of the D/A converter, a high output is generated by the comparator.
The AND gate is enabled allowing the clock pulses to be applied to the Up Counter. As long as the comparator output is high, the Up Counter will continue counting up.
Once the counter contains a binary number equal to the analog input, the counter is disabled by a low to the AND gate.
The clear input sets the counter to zero before another conversion takes place.
An analog sine wave input produces a stepped digital output.
The advantage of this A/D converter is that it has less components compared to a simultaneous A/D converter.
The disadvantage is that more time is required to convert analog signals to digital.
This circuit is a tracking A/D converter...................
The circuit operates much like a stairstep A/D converter except the counter counts up and down.
A high output allows the counter to count up. A low output allows the counter to count down.
A tracking A/D converter continuously tracks an analog input.
The advantage of a tracking A/D converter is fast conversion requiring less circuitry.

Now, let's look at two types of digital to analog converters.
This is a binary weighted input D/A converter..............
The analog voltage output is taken from the voltage developed across Rout.
The voltage across Rout depends on the current flow. The higher the current, the greater the voltage output.
The current flow through Rout is the sum of the currents in R, 2R, 4R and 8R parallel branches.
Each of the four resistors have a value that is weighted in binary.
The LSD digit from the register has the highest resistance.
When QA is high, the current produced is the lowest which adds the least amount of voltage drop across Rout.
When QA is low, no current flow is produced in the 8R branch which adds no voltage drop across Rout.
The MSD digit from the register has the lowest resistance.
When QD is high, the current produced is the highest which adds the greatest amount of voltage drop across Rout.
Each of the 16 output combinations from the register produces a different voltage across Rout.
The advantage of this D/A converter is that it is simultaneous.
The disadvantage is that it takes a different value resistor for each output. An 8 bit converter requires 8 resistors with values from R to 128R.
This is a R/2R D/A converter or ladder converter...........
The eight resistors form a series-parallel circuit. The total resistance determines the analog voltage output.
With all 0's from the register, 0 volts are produced. The equivalent circuit is shown.
With all 1's from the register, maximum voltage will be produced. The equivalent circuit is shown.
Each of the 16 output combinations from the register produces a different voltage output.
The advantage of this D/A converter is that it uses only two values of resistors.
What type of D/A converter is shown in this circuit?

Data selector circuits have four inputs and one output.....
DISCUSSION
These circuits are used to select a specific input when more than one input is applied.
Data distributor circuits have one input and four outputs.
They are used to distribute one specific output when more than one output is available.
A data selector has four data inputs. Each input is high or low.
Two address inputs are used to select the data that is sent to the output.
If A1 and A2 are 0, then the data on input A is sent to the output.
If A1 is 1 and A2 is 0, then the data on input B is sent to the output.
If A1 is a 0 and A2 is a 1, then the data on input C is sent to the output.
If both A1 and A2 are a 1, then the data on input D is sent to the output.
For example, this data selector circuit chooses which input device is used.
Multiplexing is accomplished by addressing each input during one time period.
A counter is added to the circuit and its output is used as address inputs.
MULTIPLEX - Multiplexing is the process of putting information from several sources onto a single line or transmission path.

Now let's look at data distributors........................
A data distributor has one data input and more than one output. The input data is 1, 0 or multiplexed..
Two address inputs are used to distribute the data to one of the four outputs.
If A1 and A2 are 0, then data on the input is sent to output A.
If A1 is 1 and A2 is 0, then data on the input is sent to output B.
If A1 is a 0 and A2 is a 1, then data on the input is sent to output C.
If both A1 and A2 are a 1, then data on the input is sent to output D.
For example, this data distributor circuit chooses which output device is used.
Demultiplexing is accomplished by adding a counter to the circuit..
DEMULTIPLEX - Demultiplexing is the process of putting information from a single source onto several output paths.
The output of the counter is used as address inputs to the data distributor.
The first clock pulse sets the counter to 00, addressing output A. Touch NEXT to observe the operation.
The second clock pulse sets the counter to 01, addressing output B. Touch NEXT to observe the operation.
The third clock pulse sets the counter to 10, addressing output C. Touch NEXT to observe the operation.
The fourth clock pulse sets the counter to 11, addressing output D. Touch NEXT to observe the operation.
All four bits of data on the input have been separated to different outputs.
